questions.topic: Social Business Model with Dr. Narendra Shah
questions.question: What distinguishes a social business model from a purely commercial one?

options.text: Social businesses must always be non-profit and cannot charge customers
Social businesses explicitly integrate a social or environmental mission alongside commercial viability
Social businesses do not require a revenue model
Social businesses operate exclusively in government-sponsored sectors

questions.explanation: Social businesses deliberately embed a social or environmental purpose into their business model and measure success on both impact metrics and financial sustainability.

questions.question: The 'Customer Relationships' block in the Business Model Canvas describes:

options.text: The employment contracts between the company and its staff
The type of relationship the company establishes and maintains with each customer segment
Legal agreements with suppliers and partners
The CRM software tool the company uses

questions.explanation: Customer Relationships in the BMC describes the nature of the interaction with customers — self-service, personalised support, community, co-creation — and how relationships are acquired, retained, and grown.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'servant leadership' in an entrepreneurial context?

options.text: A leader who prioritises their own advancement above the team's needs
A leader who focuses on enabling, empowering, and removing obstacles for the team
A leader who gives all strategic decisions to employees without guidance
A leader who follows every instruction from investors without question

questions.explanation: Servant leaders see their primary role as supporting their team — providing resources, removing blockers, and enabling people to do their best work — rather than commanding from above.

questions.question: A 'freemium' business model generates revenue by:

options.text: Charging all users the same monthly fee regardless of usage
Offering a free basic tier to attract users and converting a proportion to a paid premium tier
Providing all features free of charge and monetising only through advertising
Charging once upfront for permanent access with no recurring revenue

questions.explanation: Freemium gives away a functional free version to grow a large user base, then monetises by converting a subset of users to paid tiers with advanced features or higher usage limits.

questions.question: Porter's Five Forces framework evaluates competitive intensity in an industry by examining which five forces?

options.text: Cost, quality, speed, service, and innovation
Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, bargaining power of buyers, bargaining power of suppliers, threat of substitutes
Revenue growth, margin expansion, capital efficiency, market size, and regulatory risk
Leadership, culture, strategy, execution, and funding

questions.explanation: Porter's Five Forces analyses an industry's structural attractiveness by examining the rivalry among competitors, the threat from new entrants and substitutes, and the relative power of customers and suppliers.

questions.question: In the Business Model Canvas, 'Revenue Streams' describes:

options.text: The river networks near the company's manufacturing plant
The ways in which the company generates cash from each customer segment
Only one-time product sales
The company's bank account transaction history

questions.explanation: Revenue Streams in the BMC describes how a company monetises its value propositions — through asset sales, usage fees, subscriptions, licensing, commissions, advertising, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a company 'stuck in the middle' as described by Porter?

options.text: A company that is the clear cost leader in its industry
A niche luxury brand with a focused differentiation strategy
A company that cannot claim either the lowest cost or a distinctly superior product
A startup that has achieved product-market fit in a defined segment

questions.explanation: Being 'stuck in the middle' means having neither a cost advantage nor a meaningful differentiation — making the company vulnerable to both cost leaders below and differentiators above.

questions.question: Building a strong organisational culture as an entrepreneur primarily involves:

options.text: Writing a long culture document and filing it with HR
Consistently modelling the values, behaviours, and standards you want the organisation to embody
Hiring only experienced managers from large corporations
Avoiding any discussion of values in the workplace

questions.explanation: Culture is shaped by the founder's daily behaviour and decision-making. Employees observe what leaders do, not just what they say — consistent modelling is the most powerful culture-building tool.
